--- Page 9 --- PROBLEM STATEMENT

LLMs exhibit performance degradation on long contexts due to attention dilution, leading to reduced accuracy, higher token usage, and increased latency.

Our goal is to design a lightweight hybrid retrieval and external memory architecture to mitigate context degradation while improving efficiency and response quality.

--- Page 10 --- OBJECTIVES

Demostrate Context Degradation Side-by-side comparison of standard full-context LLM vs hybrid RAG on the same document and query

Build Hybrid Retrieval Pipeline Combine BM25+FAISS in parallel, merge via RRF refine with cross-encoder reranking

Reduce Token Usage & Latency Query/response caching with LRU+TTL Target: ~60% token reduction vs baseline

Cross-Platform Memory Extension Chrome extension capturing conversations from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude.ai.

Modular, Evaluable System FastAPI backend + React frontend enabling quantitative comparison of retrieval strategies.

Evaluate Retrieval & Generation Quality Measure retrieval accuracy, context relevance, answer quality

--- Page 11 --- Investigate context degradation in long-context LLMs and empirically evaluate attention dilution and the lost-in-the-middle phenomenon.
Develop a hybrid retrieval pipeline combining BM25 + FAISS in parallel, fused via RRF and refined using cross-encoder reranking to combine lexical and semantic signals.
Implement query-level and response-level caching using LRU + TTL to reduce redundant computation and improve interactive document QA latency.
Target: reduction in token usage against a full-context baseline and evaluate precision improvements on keyword-heavy queries over semantic-only retrieval.
Extend the architecture toward cross-platform conversational memory using a Chrome extension to capture and inject relevant context across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude.ai.

CONCLUSION
